title: If a Load Shifts on a Journey
whatItIs: If your load moves, slow down, stop safely and resecure it if it's safe. If it falls into the road or is dangerously unstable, stop, call 999 and wait for help.

keyFacts.text: If the load has shifted but is still on the vehicle, you MUST slow down and avoid heavy braking and steering.
You MUST NOT continue the journey until the load is secure.

keyFacts: Never try to retrieve a load from a motorway, dual carriageway or any road where you might be in danger.

visual.caption: Load shifting or lost: what to do

items.title: Check it safely
items.text: Don't walk under a leaning load.

items.title: Resecure if it's safe
items.text: Only if it's safe. Avoid risks like working at height.

items.title: Load in the road? Call 999
items.text: Report it to the police and wait for help.

a.label: Load shifted, still on board
points: Slow down, avoid harsh braking and steering
Stop safely and resecure if it's safe

b.label: Load off or dangerously unstable
points: Stop in a safe place as soon as possible

onTheTest.question: Part of your load falls onto a dual carriageway. What should you do?
options: Stop on the carriageway and pick it up quickly
Stop in a safe place, call 999 and wait for help
Drive on and report it at the end of your shift
Ask other drivers to help you collect it
onTheTest.why: Stop in a safe place, call 999 and wait for the emergency services or highway authorities. Don't retrieve a load from a road where you might be in danger.

onTheTest.question: You arrive at a delivery and find the load has shifted. What should happen?
options: Drive back to the depot to reload
Quarantine the vehicle until there's a safe unloading plan
Release all the lashings at once
Unload by hand as quickly as possible
onTheTest.why: The vehicle should be quarantined on site until a safe unloading plan is made. A known unstable 'shot load' must not go back on the public road.

traps: Open vehicle: don't release lashings until you're sure the load is stable.
Load might be leaning on the rear doors? Check it from the side.
In a live lane or on the hard shoulder, contact the police or highway authority.
